Ocea: Listen, don’t tell her we said this, for Pete’s sake, but just get her off to drama school. Her name flings itself off into the performing abyss and where it is headed exactly is anyone’s guess. Can she sing? No matter if she can’t, she’ll be right. Don’t let her sign her own contracts though – paperwork and officialdom are not her caper! So, get her an agent and hopefully a good one.
Ocean: Be it to a romantic interest, a career or an answer to a seemingly simple question, Ocean is nearly impossible to pin down.
Oceana:
Pardon the pun but can she swim? 
Yes. 
Good. Can she count? 
Yes.
Is she a scientist? 
Shit no. 
Is she a little bit shy? 
Yes. 
Is it her parents fault? 
Yes, yes it is. 
Is the happy? 
…Mmmm, she will be soon. She just hasn’t figured out what she wants yet. She will.
October: October never shaves, which is fine by us up here in the commentary box. All we wish for is that people do what ever it is that makes them comfortable without hurting others. October certainly won't. She's a hippie, she's a pacifist and the only person she would consider hurting is this unfortunate police officer, who is currently trying to unshackle the chain she's used to attach herself to this giant, 2000 year old tree.
Odette: How I miss the halcion days of travel before planes took over. Why are we in such a rush to get to the other side of the planet now? Isn't is it so that every second is a journey, filled with as much fun and mystery as you wish to inject into it? Odette is like that. As a dignified old luxury liner she carries her guests across oceans, providing a changing scene most seconds of every day, reminding us to laugh, to sleep and to mingle with our friends. She steers us around bad weather although she'll tear straight into it if she has no choice and, most important, she reminds us to be good to mother earth. Thank you Odette.
Olana: "That's enough TV, girl! Time to get outside and move that body!!" (Note: she is the current record holder for the girl who can shove the most number of chocolates in her mouth at once.)
Olena:
Why is it hard not to envisage Olena in a Parisian flat, lying naked on a couch and getting her breath back while her lover is in the kitchen making her a fresh lemon and iced water. The tall 3rd storey windows are open, allowing a spring breeze to sway the lace curtains gently and to cool her damp skin, while the lazy saturday afternoon traffic outside begins to lull her into sleep.
Amen.
Olenka:
Man, those Eastern European girls pack some punch, don't they? In a past life Olenka was a squadron leader in the Russian air force. Her and her trusty Yak downed more Messerschmitts than almost any other pilot. A newspaper reporter went to interview her one afternoon after another successful sortie. They caught up with her at the bar. She was still dressed in her flight gear, smoking a cigarette and drinking a vodka, straight up. 
“Squadron Leader Olenka, can I talk to you about today's mission and how it's all going, so I can tell our comrades of how well we're doing?" the reporter asked, rather timidly,  
"Sonny, if you buy me a drink I'll tell you whatever you like. Otherwise leave me alone and let me do my job."
Amen.
Olga: Olga is big and tough, and as an Olympic discus thrower from St Petersburg, Russia, she needs to be.
Olimpia: You know those big weddings that require several caterers, not to mention a veritable events organiser, given the number of people attending? Well this is the space in which Olimpia is in her element. It's an arena for scandalous gossip surrounded by old family money, for get-togethers with a myriad of friends and family who she almost never gets to see in the same place at the same time, for wearing new ornate dresses that cost her husband an arm and a leg, and for squeezing the cheek of God-knows how many grandchildren. Yep, the noise of such a place drives many people insane, but not our Olimpia. The bigger and the louder the better. As for the clean-up, well don't worry. Daddy organised a company to take care of that too.
Olive: “Olive, I have a problem,” you say, and she sits quietly and listens while you tell her your woes. After you have finished she leans forward and takes your hands in hers, and explains how it is, how the world works, and what you can do to make your problem go away. Thankyou Olive.
Olivia:
Should we describe Olivia as a drama queen? Indeed, is it fair to describe anyone as drama queen?
We think it is. Why? Because if no one cried out and carried on, needlessly garnering attention and diverting the spotlight, how boring would life be? Imagine living in a world where no one complained, where no one shouted their euphoria from the top of a mountain at the top of their lungs? It’d be like everyone living in Switzerland where nothing outlandish happens, where all trains run on time and where no one is late for work.  
Life, remember, is a collected blend of light and shade, of noise and heat, of humour and tragedy, and thank Christ people like Olivia here exist, is all we can say. 
So, does Olivia carry on and sulk for no reason sometimes? …Sure.
Does she get excited over the littlest things? …Yep.
Would life be dull without her? …I bloody-well guarantee it. 
Amen.
Olwyn:
Olwyn rhymes with, “What, another one? Oh well....alright then.”
As a phrase muttered regularly by midwives, secretaries and personal assistants all over the planet, daily, without her the modern world would surely struggle.
Oonagh:
"What? You don't like that?" Oonagh asks through gritted teeth. The man who just told her he wanted to break up with her is currently in agony, lying on the ground with her foot on his neck, his left arm twisted horribly up behind his back. She might snap it at the shoulder, we're not sure. "....are you suuuuure you want to do that?"

He stutters. He tries to speak. He grimaces more and then he mutters, "......aaah....well.....now that I come to think about it....."
Ophelia: Ophelia is a curvaceous woman who seduces young men by telling them that she never wears any knickers.
Oprah: The name of a huge dining table made out of solid American Oak. She was built where she sits and it takes 10 men to move her now, but by god has she seen some sights? She’s had food and all manner of booze tossed all over her, presidents, queens and the odd homeless person have feasted in her presence, and raunchy guests have fornicated on and under her.
Oriana: God, has Oriana ever worked a week in her life? Ah, I see, she helped her dad run the vegie shop when she was a little girl. Well I suppose that's something. Then she married that shipping magnate and after her divorce she won't be working anytime soon. She'll be too busy getting ready for that annual ball in Monaco. She's met the prince, you know. She likes him. He thinks Oriana is fun, but she's loud when she's drunk, and you need to keep it together at these kinds of events.
Oriel: Yes, she's dignified and lovely, whether in public or in private - very insightful, as a matter of fact - and she’s excellent company all round. And that's the thing about Oriel: she always leaves you feeling like she has more to tell or has more laughs to provide, and that you're missing out by not experiencing them. Do you know what I mean?....
Orijana: The name of a cruise ship who is being skippered by a drunk Italian. What does that mean?…..It means ANYTHING IS POSSIBLE, and I'd keep a life-jacket handy.
Orla: Orla is waiting for her cliched Prince Charming to arrive and gobble her up, though you’d never imagine that by observing her behaviour. She works hard and is a fine delegator. In fact, she has become a bit cynical about the whole ‘Mr Right’ thing. (Don’t give up honey. They’re out there - Management.)
Ornella: Ornella greets strangers like long-lost loves. She adores big gatherings and intimate evenings, and no one believes she actually goes to a thing called work.
Ottilia: I tell ya', Ottilia, how is it that every time you tell a story it takes off like a runaway train? The truth - well, never let it get in the way, as she'll tell you. But, despite her apparently mixed up and slightly confused approach to this thing we call life, she's excellent company and she drives a nice car. Is it hers?
